response.final_text:
**Proposed disposition:** CLOSE_FP, confidence 0.6. A human analyst still has to decide it.

**Three facts that drove it:**
1. The trader bought 1333 by market order at 13:16:57, at 10003–10004. They sold the same 1333 by market at 9998 at 13:17:17. That closes the position at a loss: round trip −5.42 ticks, price move −2 ticks, reversion 0.
2. There was no benefit from the opposite-side sale (feature b). The price did not move in the trader's favour, and it did not revert after the cancel.
3. Three BUY limits of 4800 (14400 in total, 5.7x depth, each about 1.9x) sat 6 ticks from the touch. All three were cancelled 600 ms after the sell, with no fills. Nothing else points to spoofing: no other pattern of this kind in the session and no prior alerts on this trader. No single order reached 3x depth.

**What would change my mind:** Evidence that the bids pushed the price up before the sell, or a reversion after the cancel. A pattern repeating across other sessions would also change it. I read only this window, not other sessions.

The stop-out explanation fits the sale well but the stacked bids less well, so Level 2 may want a look at why the trader stacked large bids while long.
